description:
Issue summary: Customer reports opaque 429s from batch import jobs that run intermittently (10–20 RPS bursts for ~30s every 10 minutes). Console shows available burst credits and per-route quota sufficient, but requests are being rejected at the edge with 429s.

Impact: Several import jobs fail mid-window; retries are escalated into large backoff waves and increase job completion time from minutes to hours. Affects one enterprise dedicated tenant during nightly processing.

Environment: dedicated deployment, prod-us-west, private VPC peering to customer ingress. Model: redwood/gpt-medium-v1.

Observed behavior: Customer sees 429 responses from edge-proxy with header X-RateLimit-Reason: window-exhausted. Console credit graph does not decrement corresponding to the rejections and shows available credits. Edge logs show short refill interval (5s) while control plane policy is configured for 60s refill.

Expected behavior: Console and edge should agree on refill interval and token accounting so that transient low-frequency bursts are absorbed by burst credits and not prematurely rejected.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Use a single API key tied to the customer's dedicated pool.
2) Post a burst of 12 concurrent embedding/generation calls (short payloads) for ~25s, spaced every 10 minutes.
3) Observe 429 responses from the edge after ~18–22s into the burst for ~8–12s windows.
4) Check console quota UI and timing; console shows credits still available.

Logs / excerpts:
EDGE LOG: [2026-03-10T03:12:22Z] conn=28 path=/v1/generate key=cus-XXX status=429 reason=window-exhausted refill_interval=5s
CONTROL PLANE POLICY: tenant_refill_interval=60s policy_version=v3.4.2
CONSOLE: burst_credits_available=1200 last_refill=2026-03-10T03:11:00Z
steps_to_reproduce: Authenticate with the tenant's API key
Trigger 12 concurrent short generation/embedding requests for ~25s
Observe 429s surfaced from the edge at ~20s into burst
Compare console burst_credits and edge logs for refill_interval and reason header
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: edge-proxy config drift after a recent hotfix left a legacy refill schedule (5s) active on the edge nodes while the control plane operates on 60s windows. This creates misaligned token buckets where edge depletes local window tokens faster and returns 429s without consulting the central burst pool. Correlated with a deploy on 2026-03-09 23:40 UTC that updated edge-side rate-limiter binary to 1.8.1-hotfix.

What we've checked so far: 
- Pulled edge-proxy config from a sample node; refill_interval=5000ms found (should be 60000ms).
- Console policy in DB shows correct 60s setting.
- No tenant-level rate-rule overrides in console.
- Replayed traffic in staging with aligned windows reproduces no 429s.

Next steps: coordinate with infra to push corrected edge config or rollback the hotfix; add a one-off metric to count edge-vs-control refill_interval mismatch; examine if stale config can survive node restarts or requires a rolling restart.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:15 - Aisha Khan (Support): Customer reported repeated 429s during scheduled imports starting 2026-03-10 03:10 UTC. Attached example request IDs and edge logs. Asked for immediate triage.

2026-03-10 10:02 - Diego Morales (SRE): Confirmed edge node config shows refill_interval=5s on four nodes. Opened INT-404 to track hotfix rollback and node restart. Asked customer to pause retries for the import job to avoid cascade.

2026-03-10 11:30 - Customer (CloudScale Analytics): Able to pause and shift job schedule. They reported business impact as delayed analytics but no data loss. Asked whether this will impact other tenants sharing same edge cluster.

2026-03-10 12:45 - Lina Park (Platform Eng): Hotfix 1.8.1-hotfix introduced an environment variable override for EDGE_REFILL_MS that was not populated in the deploy pipeline; rolling restart will pick correct value. Preparing a safe, staged restart plan for affected edge nodes in us-west.

2026-03-11 02:20 - Diego Morales (SRE): Performed staged restart of 6/6 affected edge pods. Verified refill_interval now 60000ms. Retested with customer's burst pattern in a shadow run; no 429s observed. Patching rolling restart to remaining nodes tonight.

2026-03-12 08:05 - Support (Aisha Khan): Followed up with the customer, suggested gradual job resume and recommended client-side exponential backoff with jitter as interim. Customer asked for confirmation that billing/credit counts will be reconciled; escalated to Billing (linked SUP-71234).
resolution_notes: In Progress: SRE rolled back the edge hotfix override by updating EDGE_REFILL_MS and performing staged restarts; affected edge nodes now match control plane policy. Temporary mitigation: customer paused scheduled retries and resumed at lower concurrency. Follow-up action: add automated config drift alert and add an end-to-end test that exercises refill sync between control plane and edge on deploys. Billing reconciliation request opened (SUP-71234).
recommended_workaround: Pause high-frequency retries and resume imports at lower concurrency (<=6 concurrent connections) until edge nodes confirm correct refill interval. Implement client-side exponential backoff with jitter to avoid synchronized retry waves.
follow_up_actions: Add CI gating test to validate EDGE_REFILL_MS parity with control-plane policy on deploy
Create an alert when edge-config-refill != control-plane-refill for any tenant
Coordinate with Billing to reconcile perceived credit consumption (SUP-71234)
